mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand with partial offset from housing activity, resulting in muted but positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 2% YoY and HOUST rises > 1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero in triggered episodes (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below -0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index above 2% monthly signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above 0.4% for three consecutive months signals improving household purchasing power, which boosts consumer demand and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in average hours worked (proxied by HOUST) signals both headcount and hours contraction, which reduces aggregate labor input and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and HOUST falls in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and cash flows, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
